items.title: Contents opens a wrapping chip row, not a panel
items.observation: Contents injected 71 nodes as a wrapping inline module strip and displaced the lesson.
items.user_impact: The navigation becomes harder to scan and will degrade as modules grow.
evidence: Interaction walk reproduced a nine-chip strip wrapping to two rows.
00-evidence-contents-menu-annotated.jpg
items.cause: Module navigation is conditionally rendered inside the lesson flow.
items.recommendation: Use a named, focus-managed contents disclosure or drawer.
acceptance_checks: Contents exposes a named navigation region without unexpected lesson displacement.

items.title: Thirty-two states share one URL
items.observation: Lesson navigation did not update the URL.
items.user_impact: Learners cannot bookmark or share a particular lesson or use browser history between lessons.
evidence: All lesson states retained the same page URL.
items.cause: Lesson identity exists only as internal state.
items.recommendation: Encode lesson identity in a stable route, query, or hash contract.
acceptance_checks: A copied lesson URL opens the same lesson and back-forward traverses lessons.

items.title: Keyboard unserved and focus styles absent
items.observation: Arrow keys did not navigate and source contained no explicit focus rules.
items.user_impact: Keyboard users receive weak location and accelerated-navigation feedback.
evidence: ArrowLeft and ArrowRight produced no lesson navigation.
Source contained zero focus selectors in the sampled audit.
items.cause: No explicit course-level keyboard and focus contract was implemented.
items.recommendation: Verify visible native focus and add optional non-conflicting course shortcuts.
acceptance_checks: Every control has visible focus and all course tasks are keyboard operable.

items.title: No landmarks or live lesson announcement
items.observation: The dynamic page used generic containers with no landmarks or live region.
items.user_impact: Assistive-technology users receive weaker orientation when lessons change.
evidence: DOM inspection found zero header, nav, main, footer, or live-region elements.
items.cause: The single-page shell has no semantic structure or transition announcement contract.
items.recommendation: Add semantic regions and announce or focus the new lesson heading once.
acceptance_checks: The accessibility tree exposes semantic regions and announces each lesson change once.

items.title: Windows-only font stack
items.observation: The declared type choices were interpreted as unavailable outside Windows.
items.user_impact: The original report predicted inconsistent rendering across platforms.
evidence: Source declared Cambria and Calibri before common fallbacks.
items.cause: Platform-named fonts were treated as proof of unavailable rendered fonts.
items.recommendation: Use cross-platform stacks or self-host intended faces.
acceptance_checks: Rendered type is verified on representative platforms.

items.title: Six-to-seven font sizes and bold as the default voice
items.observation: Page one rendered eight distinct font sizes and lesson states used many bold roles.
items.user_impact: Excessive type roles can weaken hierarchy and make the interface feel mechanically assembled.
evidence: Fresh run measured eight distinct sizes on page one.
01-lesson-before-annotated.jpg
items.cause: Text styling is assigned per element instead of through a small semantic scale.
items.recommendation: Reduce type roles only where hierarchy and reading tests support it.
acceptance_checks: Representative lesson and quiz states retain clear hierarchy with fewer semantic type roles.

items.title: Dead viewport on lesson states
items.observation: Nine of twenty-one measured pages filled only 45 to 58 percent of the available region.
items.user_impact: Short lesson states can appear top-heavy or unfinished on desktop.
evidence: Per-page measurements found nine low-fill lesson states.
01-lesson-before-annotated.jpg
items.cause: Every state uses top-aligned composition regardless of content height.
items.recommendation: Use state-aware vertical composition without harming long lessons or mobile reading.
acceptance_checks: Short lesson states feel intentional while long and mobile states remain scroll-safe.

items.title: No search across thirty-two states of reference material
items.observation: The course exposed no full-text lookup control.
items.user_impact: The original report predicted long rule-lookup paths at a physical table.
evidence: Control inventory contained no search action.
items.cause: Course content is navigated only through modules and sequential steps.
items.recommendation: Add search after content extraction and routing.
acceptance_checks: A learner can locate a named rule quickly from an arbitrary lesson.

items.title: All-caps letterspaced kickers on every heading
items.observation: Repeated headings used small all-caps letterspaced labels.
items.user_impact: The pattern was suspected of making the course feel templated.
evidence: Repeated rendered kicker labels were observed throughout lesson states.
items.cause: A repeated editorial convention was treated as a generic visual tell.
items.recommendation: Keep or change the convention based on product voice and reading hierarchy.
acceptance_checks: The convention supports rather than competes with lesson hierarchy.

items.title: Play audio produces no visible response
items.observation: The audio label did not change during two sampled operations.
items.user_impact: A learner may not know whether speech started, failed, or is unsupported.
evidence: Two operations produced no visible label or state change; one speech probe was inconclusive.
items.cause: Speech capability and lifecycle are not exposed as explicit UI states.
items.recommendation: Expose supported, playing, stopped, unavailable, and error states.
acceptance_checks: Every speech outcome produces truthful visible and accessible feedback.

items.title: Four text and background pairs fail contrast
items.observation: The audit initially counted four contrast failures, while its own detail excluded one alpha-compositing artifact.
items.user_impact: Three genuine small-text roles are harder to read for low-vision users.
evidence: Gold on green measured 3.45:1.
Green on gold measured 3.45:1.
Muted text on cream measured 3.44:1.
items.cause: Brand colors are reused for normal-sized text without role-specific variants.
items.recommendation: Create accessible text variants while preserving the palette.
acceptance_checks: All normal text and control labels meet 4.5:1 in tested states.

items.title: Course content is trapped inside React components
items.observation: One 760-line, 86,582-character file fused content, state, rendering, speech, and styles.
items.user_impact: Routing, search, print material, semantic structure, and consistent tokens share one expensive change surface.
evidence: Source inspection counted 256 inline style attributes in the monolithic page.
items.cause: Content, state, platform capabilities, and view concerns have no module boundaries.
items.recommendation: Extract stable content data, routing/state, semantic shell, capability adapters, and visual roles without requiring a framework rewrite.
acceptance_checks: Lesson content and route state are independently testable while all thirty-two lessons retain behavior.

items.title: One-page printable cheat card
items.observation: No concise table-side reference is exposed.
items.user_impact: A learner lacks a compact aid during a real game.
evidence: Product frame identifies physical-table performance as the post-course job.
items.cause: The course is optimized for sequential learning rather than table-side recall.
items.recommendation: Create a print-ready one-page reference after content extraction.
acceptance_checks: One printed page covers the highest-value rules and remains legible.

items.title: Rule search and jump to term
items.observation: The interface has no full-text term lookup.
items.user_impact: Terms that do not match module titles may take longer to retrieve.
evidence: Control inventory contained no search; the Joker lookup still succeeded in three operations.
items.cause: Course content is not exposed through a searchable data model.
items.recommendation: Add term search if unmatched-term task evidence justifies it.
acceptance_checks: Unmatched terms resolve to the relevant lesson with a measurable improvement.

items.title: Per-module deep links
items.observation: Individual modules cannot be linked directly.
items.user_impact: A teacher or peer cannot send a learner to a precise module.
evidence: All module navigation retained one URL.
items.recommendation: Include module links in the routing contract.
acceptance_checks: A copied module link opens the correct module.

items.title: 375-pixel mobile pass
items.observation: The original environment could not run a 375-pixel responsive verification.
items.user_impact: The likely table-side device remained unverified.
evidence: Coverage ledger recorded 375-pixel emulation as blocked.
items.cause: Responsive browser capability was unavailable in that run.
items.recommendation: Run all templates and navigation states at 375 by 812.
acceptance_checks: No overflow or unusable wrapping appears at 375 by 812.

items.title: Surface the resume state
items.observation: The app restores progress silently without telling the learner.
items.user_impact: A valuable repeat-use feature is invisible and offers no start-over choice.
evidence: Behavioral reload test confirmed resume but the interface exposed no resume message.
items.cause: Persistence is implemented as hidden behavior rather than an explicit return state.
items.recommendation: Offer resume and start-over choices when saved progress exists.
acceptance_checks: Returning learners see the saved position and can resume or start over.
